parsed.justification: All standard policy sections are present (header, purpose, scope, principles, roles, detailed requirements, monitoring, training, exceptions, compliance, enforcement, references, approval) with technically accurate alignment to NIST SP 800-63B (length floors, no periodic expiry, blocklisting, rate limiting, AAL3 phishing-resistance, activation-secret 10-attempt cap) and CSF 2.0/ISO 27001 mappings. Internal consistency is strong: domain separation, smart-card-first, and MFA requirements reinforce each other across sections, and local hardening parameters (e.g., 14/20/24/32 chars, stricter timeouts) are explicitly flagged as exceeding rather than contradicting baselines.
evidence_quotes: User passwords must not be changed on a fixed periodic schedule solely because time has elapsed.
Centrally verified password used with MFA | 14 characters minimum | Local military hardening above the NIST minimum of 8 characters
Activation secrets are limited to no more than 10 consecutive failed attempts.

parsed.justification: The policy is deeply tailored to this exact organisation: it explicitly addresses NATO classification domains (NU/NR/NS/MISSION SECRET), NATO directives (C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015/1029), SHAPE operational control, Romanian host-nation law, SOFA limits, SCIF/COMSEC/CDS contexts, J6/ISSM chain, and threat-specific concerns like APT, kinetic-cyber contingency, and classification spillage. Generic boilerplate is essentially absent — sector, jurisdiction, size (40-hour training, exercises), and operational constraints are visible throughout.
evidence_quotes: Credentials must not be reused across NU, NR, NS, MISSION SECRET, national, coalition, contractor, or personal systems.
require two-person access for NS, MISSION SECRET, CDS, identity, COMSEC-support, and SOC systems
Authentication attempts during kinetic-cyber contingency periods.

parsed.justification: Citations are pervasive and precise throughout the policy, referencing specific NIST CSF 2.0 subcategories (PR.AA-01/03/05, PR.AT-01/02, PR.PS-01), NIST SP 800-63B verifier requirements, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A clauses (5.15, 5.17, 5.18, 8.5), GDPR Article 32, NIS2 Article 21(2)(j), and named NATO documents (C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015, AC/35-D/1029, AC/322-D(2017)0009, Cyber Defence Pledge). Critically, the policy explicitly flags unsupported items rather than fabricating—e.g., NATO controlled-document clauses are marked as 'unsupported in this draft' and local hardening parameters (14/20/24/32 chars, history of 10) are openly labelled as not externally prescribed.
evidence_quotes: NIST SP 800-63B sets an 8-character floor when password is used as part of MFA.
NATO classification separation — exact NATO clause unsupported in this draft.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO/IEC 27002:2022 | Annex A 5.15 Access Control, 5.16 Identity Management, 5.17 Authentication Information, 5.18 Access Rights, 8.5 Secure Authentication, 8.15 Logging.

parsed.justification: The controls align well with the stated resource envelope: a 25-FTE security team and existing 24/7 theatre SOC support the monitoring requirements; PKI smart cards, vaults, COMSEC two-person integrity, SCIF, and CDS already exist in the profile and are leveraged rather than newly required. Where strong controls cannot be met, the policy provides defensible compensating controls and time-bound exception paths, and it explicitly accommodates legacy systems, national overlays, and SOFA/GDPR constraints.
evidence_quotes: Password and credential compromise scenarios must be included in at least two annual cyber exercises and one annual red-team or purple-team engagement.
Compensating controls may include: MFA or smart-card enforcement. Network isolation. Privileged-access workstation requirement. Increased SOC monitoring.

If a national system connected to the mission requires periodic password rotation by national rule, that rule may be followed on that national system, but the account must still comply with this policy's domain-separation, MFA, and blocklisting requirements.

parsed.justification: The policy systematically addresses the major applicable frameworks: NATO directives (C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015, AC/35-D/1029, AC/322-D(2017)0009, Cyber Defence Pledge), NIST CSF 2.0 and SP 800-63B, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, GDPR Article 32, NIS2 Article 21, and acknowledges Romanian CSL and SOFA limitations on host-nation reach. However, NATO-specific clauses are repeatedly flagged as 'unsupported in this draft' and Romanian implementing clauses are deferred to legal adviser, leaving secondary obligations unmapped; AGID is not relevant here, and CTS handling is mentioned only in context, not addressed for password scope. Conflicts (GDPR vs SOFA, national rotation rules vs domain policy) are acknowledged but not deeply resolved.
evidence_quotes: Contractor personal data used in authentication and logging must be processed in accordance with GDPR and host-nation legal constraints, subject to SOFA limitations.

If a national system connected to the mission requires periodic password rotation by national rule, that rule may be followed on that national system, but the account must still comply with this policy's domain-separation, MFA, and blocklisting requirements.

parsed.justification: Nearly every substantive control table row and section carries an explicit 'Source / audit reference' line that names specific clauses (e.g., NIST SP 800-63B activation-secret rules, GDPR Art. 32, NIS2 Art. 21(2)(j), ISO 27001 Annex A 5.17/8.5, CSF PR.AA-05), and where multiple frameworks are cited they are distinguished rather than lumped. It falls short of 5 because NATO controlled directives (C-M(2002)49, AC/35-D/1015, AC/35-D/1029, AC/322-D(2017)0009) are repeatedly flagged as 'exact NATO clause unsupported in this draft', leaving a portion of attributions at document-level rather than clause-level.
evidence_quotes: NIST SP 800-63B requires verifiers to support long passwords, not impose additional composition rules, accept spaces and printable characters, and verify the full submitted password.
NIST CSF 2.0 PR.AA-05; ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.17 and 8.5; local risk-based parameter.

parsed.justification: The policy makes only minimal reference to the resource envelope, anchoring annual training in the stated 40-hour allocation and tying exercises/red-team to existing programs. However, there is no explicit phasing, no trade-off reasoning tied to budget or 25-FTE security staff, and ambitious controls (24/7 SOC detections, PAM vaulting, blocklist sourcing, dual-control break-glass across many systems) are asserted without visible calibration to the resource envelope.
evidence_quotes: All personnel must receive annual password and credential-security training as part of the 40-hour annual training requirement.
Password and credential compromise scenarios must be included in at least two annual cyber exercises and one annual red-team or purple-team engagement.
Where technically feasible, password history controls must prevent reuse of the last 10 passwords for the same account.
